newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks to ascend in wake of U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks to ascend in wake of U.S. markets.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to ascend in the Tuesday session after Wall Street and the Nikkei 225 futures in Chicago ended higher overnight, brokers said.
They added that import-oriented issues were likely to be bought due to the strength of the yen against the dollar.
On Monday, the Nikkei average gained 340.73 points or 1.72 percent to 20,143.51. June Nikkei futures rose 360 to 20,190.

"The surge of the yen on Monday seems to have triggered buying which alternates between blue chips and low-priced domestic-demand related stocks," said Kunihiro Hatae, Tokyo Securities general manager.

"The rally (in stocks) was surprising, showing investors that the Tokyo market may not be as feeble as everyone believes," he added. "Helped by the bullish state of the U.S. markets on Monday, Tokyo stocks should firm."

On Monday, the dollar briefly slumped to 117.60 yen before the market opened, versus a close at 120.20/30 on Friday in New York, inspiring sales of Japanese blue chips. But by the end of the session, bargain hunters had pulled Sony Corp out of negative territory, to the relief of investors.
The paper and oil sectors climbed throughout the day, as investors believed they would benefit from lower import costs.
